print_errors.text: يبدأ بالصلاة والسلام علي سيدنا محمد
print_errors.note: «علي» printed with two dots (ي) where «على» is meant; kept as printed.
Second alif carries only the hamza; the damma is on the lam (no fatha on the hamza). Kept as printed.
Final dal has shadda only, no fatha; kept as printed.

notes: p177 has no '+': p176 ends with a full stop and p177 opens with the heading «في السجود:». p180 is '+': Surat al-Ikhlas runs from p179 into p180, so the ﴿﴾ closes at the end of p179 and reopens on p180. All harakat were read from 800-1800 dpi zooms. In the lam-mim/lam-kha ligature, the mark drawn over the lam is a sukun stacked over the next letter's vowel. I wrote it as sukun + fatha (الْمَحْيَا، وَالْمَمَاتِ، الْمَسِيحِ، الْخَيْرَاتِ، الْمَسَاكِينِ، الْجَلَالِ، الْعَظِيمَ، الْحَيَّ) or sukun + damma (الْمُبَارَكَاتُ، الْمُنْكَرَاتِ) according to the tail shape. Printed vowel-less forms kept: اللَّهُمّ (p177, shadda only on the mim), رَبَّياني, سَيِّدنا (p177, no fatha on the dal), الْعَالَمِين (no fatha on the nun), عَادَيْتَ. لاَ/إِلاَّ printed with the marks on the lam-alif ligature are written لَا/إِلَّا. Ayat al-Kursi has no ayah-number ornament in the print, so none is written. The basmala in item 7 (p179) is in the ordinary unvowelled font and is written plain. The quran.py flag on p180 (أَحَدٌۢ vs 2:102) is a mis-location of a single word; it matches 112:4.
